extracted.intended_audience: International Searching Authority examiners and applicants under the PCT (International Search and Search Report preparation)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for carrying out the PCT international search and preparing the international search report and written opinion, including what to search, how to interpret claims, handling sequence listings, incorporation-by-reference, and interactions with applicants and receiving Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability requirement (requirement (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter must be capable of being used for the indicated special purpose; subject matter operating contrary to well-established physical laws (e.g., 'perpetuum mobile') or technical errors making the claimed subject matter unusable for the indicated purpose do not comply with requirement (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a motor claim complies if functioning results in mechanical movement; inability to achieve a specified characteristic (e.g., efficiency ratio) is not relevant to industrial applicability but is treated under sufficiency of description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date at which substantive requirements are verified
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of compliance with requirements (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) is carried out as of the priority date of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information incorporated into the application after the priority date that was not in the priority document cannot establish industrial applicability as of the priority date and may be new matter contrary to Articles 19(2) and 34(2)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover relevant prior art consisting of everything made available to the public anywhere by any means prior to the international filing date that can assist in determining novelty and inventive step, consulting at least the minimum documentation specified in Rule 34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISA endeavors to discover as much relevant prior art as its facilities permit and must at least consult Rule 34 minimum documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of prior art relevant to other requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ISAs are encouraged to cite prior art documents which might assist in determining whether other requirements such as sufficiency, support and industrial applicability are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documents beyond novelty/inventive step where they shed light on sufficiency or support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of differing effective dates across Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Search must recognize that designated Offices have different definitions of effective date of prior art and examiners should pick out prior art which may be relevant in Offices other than their own, without expanding beyond standard search parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such art is identified, examiners are encouraged to cite all relevant art published prior to the international filing date even if common applicants/inventors; follow Article 11(3) even if an Article 64(4) reservation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-written disclosures referenced in written documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a written disclosure refers to a non-written disclosure (oral disclosure, use, exhibition) and that written disclosure was made publicly available on or after the filing date, the search report should separately mention that fact and the date when the written disclosure was available if the underlying non-written disclosure was public before the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note separately in the search report even if the non-written disclosure does not form 'relevant prior art' in the international phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: No geographic/language/manner/age restriction for relevant prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no restriction with respect to geographical place, language or manner in which relevant information was made available, nor any age limit for documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents issued electronically are considered published provided they are retrievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who performs the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search and search report are carried out and prepared by an International Searching Authority; normally performed by one examiner but may involve two or more examiners for inventions requiring widely dispersed specialized fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign additional examiners when necessary to ensure adequate coverage across specialized fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is required to provide a written opinion on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability at the same time as establishing the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search report and written opinion inform IPEAs and designated Offices; examiners should prepare high quality reports and opinions to provide predictability for national/regional prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the search (search copy and amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search must be carried out on the basis of the search copy of the application as transmitted to the ISA by the receiving Office; there is no right to amend the application until after the international search has been established, except that obvious mistakes may be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obvious mistakes can be rectified under Rules 91.1(b)(ii),(c),(d) before the ISA begins drawing up the search report, and rectified claims will be indicated in the report (Rule 43.6bis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages marked 'INCORPORATED BY REFERENCE' should be considered as originally filed and indicated on forms; if incorporated elements are not completely contained in the priority document, note doubts in the written opinion and include additional documents ('L') relevant if re-dating were made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets stamped 'NOT TO BE CONSIDERED' should be ignored for search and examination; 'ERRONEOUSLY FILED' sheets usually need not be taken into account except in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Later-filed pages and additional fees (Rule 40bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ISA receives notification of later filed pages after beginning the search, it may invite the applicant to pay additional fees; if paid within one month, the ISA draws up the report including the later pages; if not paid, the ISA draws up the report without the later pages and remarks in the written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISA may also, when fees are paid, decide to complete a non-official international search report and written opinion based on the initially transmitted application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing compliance and invitation (Rule 13ter.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application contains nucleotide/amino acid sequences but no compliant sequence listing, the ISA may invite the applicant to furnish a compliant listing or translation within a time limit, possibly subject to a fee up to 25% of the international filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If furnished, the ISA completes the search on that basis; any sequence listing not contained in the application as filed will not form part of the international application (subject to Article 34) but may be used as a search tool; if not furnished, search only to extent meaningful without it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of search and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the filing language is not accepted by the ISA, the applicant should have supplied a translation to the receiving Office which will be used as the basis of the international search; translations of sequence listing free text may be required only for language-dependent parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office may permit language-dependent free text in more than one language; ISA may invite translation under Rule 13ter.1 and may charge a late furnishing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account earlier search results upon applicant's request
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request the ISA to take into account the results of an earlier search carried out by that or another ISA or by a national/regional Office, either by sending a copy with the search copy or by having the ISA retrieve a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISA may invite applicant to furnish copies/translations of earlier application, earlier search results, or cited documents where not transmitted by receiving Office and not available to ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to take account of earlier searches by same Authority/Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the earlier search was carried out by the same ISA or by the same Office acting as ISA, that Authority must, to the extent possible, take the results into account in establishing the international search report and written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier search relates to a priority application and was carried out by the same Office/ISA, ISA must, to the extent possible, take those results into account (Rule 41.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to take account of earlier searches by other Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the earlier search was carried out by another ISA or Office, the Authority may take the results into account if they offer a real benefit and may be considered to stand in place of at least part of the international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider fields of search and cited documents in earlier results to determine relevance and whether they improve the quality of the international search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and quality expectation of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search is essentially a thorough, high quality search of the most relevant resources and the report provides information on relevant prior art to the applicant, the public, designated Offices and IPEAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should assume some designated Offices lack systematic searching facilities and thus depend on ISAs for state of the art knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical limits on completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Although completeness is the ultimate goal, it may not be obtained because of text-search limitations, imperfections of classification systems, and economic considerations; examiners should organize the search to minimize failing to discover highly relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use most relevant resources (including IPDL databases), organize search time to reduce missing complete anticipations; lower retrieval ratio acceptable for less relevant prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of claims and orientation of the search
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must first determine the subject of the claimed invention by critically analysing the claims in light of the description and drawings; the search is directed to the invention defined by the claims interpreted with due regard to the description and drawings, with emphasis on the inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter 5 guidance on relationship between disclosure and claims; search directed to claims as filed (subject to allowed rectifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple inventions and additional search fees (unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims do not relate to one invention or a linked group forming a single general inventive concept, the applicant may be invited to pay additional search fees; if not paid, the international search will be restricted to the parts first mentioned in the claims (with limited exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional fees are paid, the parts covered thereby must also be searched; see Forms PCT/ISA/206 and related paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full coverage principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, and insofar as possible and reasonable, the international search should cover the entire subject matter to which the claims are directed or to which they might reasonably be expected to be directed after amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: functional claims that have detailed examples in the description require the search to include the detailed example; economic reasons may justify some restrictions where claims are broad and many examples exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of speculative or unduly wide claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort need be made for unduly wide or speculative claims beyond the extent they are supported by the description; extension only justified if probable that extended search could produce a document enabling a reasonable objection of lack of novelty or inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a meaningful search for unsupported scope can be carried out without much extra effort, extend search; examples provided (telephone exchange vs telegraph exchanges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: International search for independent claims must take into account the subject matter of all dependent claims; dependent claims are interpreted as restricted by features of the claims on which they depend and are considered novel if the independent claim is novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If novelty/inventive step of main claim is questioned, may need to expand search to assess dependent claim novelty; do not search for features so well known that documentary evidence is unnecessary, although a handbook can be cited if found rapidly. Dependent claims that add further features (combination claims) should be treated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of claim wording by skilled person
rubrics_metrics.description: Words of a claim must be read as understood by a person skilled in the relevant art according to their normal meaning and scope in that art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs 15.20–15.28 for guidance on interpreting particular claim types and features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part (Jepson) claims and technological background
rubrics_metrics.description: In two-part claims the preamble is a limitation and, in certain circumstances, it may be desirable to extend the search to include the 'technological background' including the preamble, state of prior art in the description, and general technological background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the preamble portion (before 'characterized by' or 'the improvement comprising') as limiting; include background where useful to locate best prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy for combination claims and sub-combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: For combination claims (e.g., A+B+C) search should be directed to the combination and concurrently to sub-combinations and individual elements (AB, AC, BC, A, B, C) in relevant classification units; searching additional units for sub-combinations or individual elements only if necessary to establish novelty for assessing inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure classification units searched cover both combination and relevant sub-combinations where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different categories of claims (product/process/etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: When application contains claims of different categories that satisfy unity, all must be included in the search; when claims are only of one category it may be desirable to include other categories in the search (e.g., process claims may require searching for the product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In chemical process claims, starting products generally form part of the state of the art and need not be searched; intermediate products searched only when claimed; final products highly recommended to be searched except when evidently known.

rubrics_metrics.name: When no meaningful search is possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners exclude from search subject matter for which no meaningful search can be made (e.g., Rule 39 exclusions or exceptional situations) and indicate reasons on the appropriate forms; lack of search result may preclude forming an opinion on novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate reasons for not establishing an international search report in Box II of Form PCT/ISA/210 or Form PCT/ISA/203 and refer to declaration in written opinion boxes as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious mistakes and matter not to be used (Rule 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner notices an obvious mistake the ISA may invite the applicant to request rectification; if matter not to be used (contrary to public order/morality etc.) is noted, ISA suggests voluntary correction and notifies receiving Office and International Bureau; corrections must not introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not correct, examiner proceeds with search covering subject matter to which claims might reasonably be expected to be directed after correction; International Bureau may omit noted matter from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information meeting Rule 48.2(l) and file access restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA is not obliged to check for information meeting Rule 48.2(l), but if it appears may suggest applicant request omission from publication; where the International Bureau has omitted information from publication or public file access, the ISA must not provide access to that information except to applicant or authorized person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISA may provide access to replacement sheets received from the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary steps: treatment of documents cited in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited in the international application should be examined if they are starting point of the invention, show the state of the art, provide alternative solutions, or are necessary for correct understanding; citations relating only to irrelevant details may be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a cited document is unpublished/not accessible and appears essential, ISA may postpone the search and request a copy; otherwise attempt the search and indicate if no meaningful search could be carried out or if the search needed restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract, title and figure considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should consider the abstract, title and figure to be published in relation to PCT Regulations and determine definitive abstract contents no later than completion of the international search report; under certain circumstances the examiner will establish the abstract/title/select the figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract is established in the language of publication or in the language of a transmitted translation under Rule 23.1(b) if the ISA so wishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification according to IPC
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering the abstract, the examiner classifies the international application according to at least the International Patent Classification (IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification is part of the search preparatory steps and guides resources/units to search.
